title: OS map work: Helvellyn and Ullswater, Lake District (1:25,000)
subject: Geography
source: Written for geography/y7 lessons 11, 12, 13 (OS map extract: Helvellyn and Ullswater, Lake District, 1:25,000 (on screen via an online OS map; portal printable))
intro: Open Helvellyn and Ullswater, Lake District on an online OS map (or a paper OS Explorer map) on screen, as in the lesson, and use it to answer these questions. Ordnance Survey maps are Crown copyright, so the extract itself is not printed here.

questions.q: Explain how a corrie forms.
questions.a: Snow collects in a hollow and becomes ice; the ice rotates, plucking the back wall and abrading the floor; when it melts a tarn may form
questions.model: Start: snow in a hollow. Then: it turns to ice. Then: ice plucks the back wall and abrades the floor. End: a deep hollow, often with a tarn.

questions.q: What forms when two corries erode back to back?
questions.a: An arete

questions.q: How do contours show a steep slope?
questions.a: Lines close together

questions.q: A feature is 6 tenths across square 3417 and 2 tenths up. Six-figure reference?
questions.model: Easting: 34 then 6 tenths: 346. Northing: 17 then 2 tenths: 172. Together: 346172.

questions.q: What is till?
questions.a: Unsorted rock and clay dropped by ice

questions.q: Which end of a drumlin faces the way the ice came from?
questions.a: The blunt (steep) end

questions.q: On a 1:25,000 map, 10 cm is how far?
questions.a: 2.5 km

questions.q: What is a ribbon lake?
questions.a: A long, narrow lake in a glaciated valley

questions.q: Name two glacial landforms you would expect near Helvellyn.
questions.a: For example: corrie (Red Tarn) and arete (Striding Edge)

questions.q: Core: Draw and label a sketch of a glaciated upland with a corrie, tarn, arete, pyramidal peak and U-shaped valley.
questions.a: A labelled sketch with all five landforms correctly placed
questions.model: Teacher shows it first: two hollows back to back on a mountain, the ridge between labelled 'arete', a lake in one labelled 'tarn'.

questions.q: Extend: Use the OS extract of Helvellyn to find Red Tarn and Striding Edge. Describe the contour pattern at each.
questions.a: Red Tarn: contours curve tightly round a hollow open to the east; Striding Edge: contours close together on both sides of a narrow ridge

questions.q: Stretch: Explain why a U-shaped valley is wider than a river valley.
questions.a: A glacier fills the whole valley and erodes the sides and floor by plucking and abrasion

questions.q: Core: Draw and label a valley glacier showing lateral, medial and terminal moraine, then a field of drumlins after the ice melted.
questions.a: Correctly placed moraines; drumlins shown as egg shapes with blunt ends up-valley
questions.model: Teacher shows it first: two glaciers joining, a dark line where they meet labelled 'medial moraine'.

questions.q: Extend: Give six-figure grid references for three features on the OS extract worksheet.
questions.a: Answers on the worksheet key (each to the nearest tenth of a square)

questions.q: Stretch: Explain how an erratic can tell us the direction the ice moved.
questions.a: Its rock type matches a source area; the line from the source to where it lies shows the ice direction

questions.q: Core: Unit quiz on the portal (12 questions: glaciers, processes, landforms, contours, grid references, scale).
questions.a: Answers in the portal quiz key
questions.model: Teacher does question 1 aloud: 'Name the process where rocks in the ice scrape the ground.' Abrasion.

questions.q: Extend: In the portal response box, describe the landscape of the OS extract in 4 sentences using grid references.
questions.a: Accurate description naming at least two landforms with grid references and the ribbon lake

questions.q: Stretch: Why should we look after landscapes like the Lake District?
questions.a: They are fragile and loved by many visitors; we are stewards of the land

questions.q: A knife-edge ridge between corries is an:
questions.a: Arete

questions.q: Big question: how can a flat map show a mountain?
questions.a: Contour lines show height: close lines for steep slopes and patterns that match landforms like corries and ridges

questions.q: A drumlin is made of:
questions.a: Till

questions.q: Big question: where does all the rock a glacier carries end up?
questions.a: It is deposited as moraine, drumlins and erratics when the ice melts

questions.q: Windermere is a:
questions.a: Ribbon lake

questions.q: Big question: how well can you read a glaciated landscape from a map?
questions.a: Answers show use of contours, grid references and scale to identify landforms
